scenarios.answer: No — the evidence contradicts that claim. EKOS's stated key invariants are that the **ledger is append-only** (knowledge is never modified in place) and that the **Runtime is read-only** — it "reconstructs and interprets state, never modifies it." The architecture is one-way: enterprise systems feed an Observation Layer that "collects facts only," and `ekos-runtime` is described elsewhere as "read-only by design invariant, RFC 0005 — this is a read." When a query is answered, `ekos ask` reads the entity's real, on-demand source text "straight from the artifact store," not by writing back to source systems. So ekos-runtime does not write directly back to enterprise source systems when answering a query, and it does not bypass the ledger — it is read-only by design.
